Japan's Industrial Production Fell in August But Expected to Rebound

TOKYO--Japan's industrial production continued to fall in August, but companies expect a rebound in the coming months on easing concerns over energy supply and solid demand related to artificial intelligence.

Industrial output fell 1.7% from the previous month, following a 0.2% decrease in July, government data showed Wednesday. That missed the 1.7% rise expected by economists in a poll by data provider Quick.
Still, Japanese companies expect industrial production to rise 3.2% in September and increase 3.1% in October, the data showed.
Factory activity is projected to recover as the Japanese government has secured alternative energy sources amid the ongoing Middle East tensions, while the AI boom continues to boost global demand.

The Bank of Japan, which is expected to raise interest rates again soon, has cited the impact of the Middle East conflict and AI demand on the economy and prices as key elements for its policy decisions.
